briefdescription.para: Global base address used for complex addressing.
Whether any complex addressing has a base register.
The scale of any complex addressing.
The list of "base" registers for this use.

detaileddescription.para:
When this is non-empty. The canonical representation of a formula is
BaseRegs.size > 1 implies ScaledReg != NULL and
ScaledReg != NULL implies Scale != 1 || !BaseRegs.empty().
The reg containing recurrent expr related with currect loop in the formula should be put in the ScaledReg. #1 enforces that the scaled register is always used when at least two registers are needed by the formula: e.g., reg1 + reg2 is reg1 + 1 * reg2. #2 enforces that 1 * reg is reg. #3 ensures invariant regs with respect to current loop can be combined together in LSR codegen. This invariant can be temporarily broken while building a formula. However, every formula inserted into the LSRInstance must be in canonical form.
This should be non-null when Scale is not zero.

briefdescription.para: An additional constant offset which added near the use.

detaileddescription.para: This requires a temporary register, but the offset itself can live in an add immediate field rather than a register.

briefdescription.para: Incorporate loop-variant parts of S into this Formula, attempting to keep all loop-invariant and loop-computable values in a single base register.
Check whether or not this formula satisfies the canonical representation.
Helper method to morph a formula into its canonical representation.

simplesect.para: Formula::BaseRegs. Every formula having more than one base register, must use the ScaledReg field. Otherwise, we would have to do special cases everywhere in LSR to treat reg1 + reg2 + ... the same way as reg1 + 1*reg2 + ... On the other hand, 1*reg should be canonicalized into reg.

briefdescription.para: Get rid of the scale in the formula.

detaileddescription.para:
In other words, this method morphes reg1 + 1*reg2 into reg1 + reg2.
true if it was possible to get rid of the scale, false otherwise.
After this operation the formula may not be in the canonical form.

briefdescription.para: Return the total number of register operands used by this formula.

detaileddescription.para: This does not include register uses implied by non-constant addrec strides.

briefdescription.para: Return the type of this formula, if it has one, or null otherwise.

detaileddescription.para: This type is meaningless except for the bit size.
